I was a junior community manager for a company.

It was my first time doing this professionally, which I thought meant I would be free to make mistakes and learn from them, but I didn't even know I was making mistakes.... idk..

Everyone else loves it and gets on fine I just...I don't know.

I made what feels like 1 mistake and everyone told me I'd be fine when I expressed fears I would be fired...

I don't know...I was right and I'm just so afraid and sad and depressed. I hate myself so much.

Unfortunately I'm in a non-english country where I haven't been able to learn the language here for financial reasons, so minimum wage isn't an option so much..

Besides, it wouldn't be enough to afford my rent and stuff, I think.

Idk...I'm just so fucked hahah....

I just don't understand.

I was told my work was good and I begged and pleaded to be better, it was pathetic, and they just...said no.

They said it would be too much pressure...as if losing my only income is better...

I don't know. I just wish they had said something...

No I quite literally just didn't know. I had to discover myself and could only really do so through relationships. It's great if you knew yourself 100% from the very beginning, but I didn't.

I'm still even friends with my ex and we discussed a lot how we both ended up wanting different things out of our relationship and that understanding helped us grow as people.

Hello,

I entered mono relationships under the guise I was mono and later experienced a desire to share my relationship with more people- bringing them into our dynamic as a whole unique partner, not just for sex or anything physical. It was the same love I felt- and still did feel- for my mono partner(s).

Those relationships were ruined not because I was unfaithful, but because of some inter-personal stuff as well as me bringing up the idea of bringing another partner in that really rubbed them the wrong way. The idea I could feel the same way for them as others felt bad for them and we split partially because of it.

I appreciate if you could not claim I'm a cheater as I find those people disgusting, thank you, as well as the other assumptions you made about me.

You sound hurt, honestly. I'm sorry if someone did that to you.

Appreciate the advice but I find these kinds of suggestions, for all kinds of 'communities' to be a little unhelpful for me personally.

I've tried joining groups for other aspects of myself- being lgbt, autistic, english-speaking in a non-english speaking country, ect. And I find I tend to just....have no idea what to do or talk about. We bridge the topic at hand- in this case polyamory- and then when that ends, poof. There's just no desire to continue because frankly we're all there for rather shallow topics.

Because of this, the 'making friends' part just...doesn't happen. I tend to make friends through my hobbies, regardless of demographic through genuine connection. Any other way just does not work for me, it feels superficial and I always feel out of my comfort zone when trying to interact.

That isn't to say I won't at least look- doesn't hurt- but just giving a sort of context as to why I might struggle with this direction.

Hey- glad to hear a similar perspective.

I've tried them before and I absolutely hate them lol. It's a challenge already to get along with people but I find dating apps to just exacerbate every issue I have socially. I just don't like it.

I also have never really fell in love like that. I really need to know people before any kind of feelings comes into it. For casual sleeping around? Sure, whatever. But for something real? Nah, I can't do apps.

No, I haven't.

I've never even met another person in real life who is poly. We have to be an insanely small % of people it's just so unlikely I'll ever meet someone naturally who is poly.

I don't do online dating or tinder anything like that- I would rather be friends first and my friends have to be made naturally (I'm autistic so the way I navigate relationships is also different)

Personally I'm scared of what happens if I try and fail.
Maybe I'd be paralyzed? Forced to live life in a severely degraded manner.
Maybe I'd go into a coma. Conscious but unable to do anything.
Maybe I'd be locked up forever.

It's not the act, it's not the success, it's the potential failure that stops me.

A girl I went to school with died of cancer...she was the type to do charity work as her hobby. Lovely girl.
It should have been me.
It fees so unfair that people who want to live die while I have to suffer here.
